newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Mayor praises model retail chain.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Mayor praises model retail chain.

text.p: Retail chains like Japan's Seven-Eleven would bring many advantages to Shanghai's chaotic commercial sector, Mayor Xu Kuangdi told a news conference on Monday.
He was speaking after a meeting of the International Business Leaders' Advisory Council, which meets once a year to advise the city government.
One of its topics this year was Shanghai as a commercial centre.

Zhang Guangsheng, chairman of the Shanghai Commerce Commission, told the meeting that retail sales in the city were growing at 23.8 percent a year, with one million square feet of floor space being added every year over the past few years. He gave no absolute figures.

Xu told reporters that, as China moved from a planned to a "socialist market economy", the existing system of state wholesalers had started to shrink but had not been replaced by a new distribution network.
This had led to confusion and chaos in the market place, causing inequity in price and quality control, inefficiency and unfair allocation of goods, he said.
He praised a speech to the meeting by Hideo Shimizu, vice-chairman of Seven-Eleven Japan Co Ltd, in which Shimizu explained the workings of his chain of convenience stores.

"If chains like this replace Mom and Pop stores, they would bring a lot of benefits," Xu said. They would protect privately or collectively owned businesses and link them in a commercial network, providing uniform prices and quality, and giving more choices to the consumer and better prices for the store operators, he added.
Such convenience stores, some of which are open 24 hours, are already operating in Shanghai but their numbers are much smaller than in other major Asian cities such as Hong Kong or Tokyo.
